back: Non-volatile storage, not directly accessed by the CPU, that keeps programs and data permanently.
Spinning magnetic platters, tracks and sectors; read/write heads use electromagnets to magnetise or detect areas.
A laser forms and reads pits and lands on a spiral track; reflection changes are read as binary.
Capacity rises CD < DVD < Blu-ray: Blu-ray's blue-violet laser has a shorter wavelength, so smaller pits.
NAND or NOR cells of transistors; electrons trapped on the floating gate (moved by the control gate) represent bits.
SSD, SD card, USB flash drive.
SSD: faster, no moving parts, durable, low power, higher cost per GB. HDD: large and cheap per GB, moving parts, slower.
Capacity, access speed, cost per GB, durability, portability.
Medium: what holds the data (disc, platter). Device: the hardware that reads/writes it (drive).
